items.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: Count Basie... says, 'what's wrong, Fab?' ... Marshall Royal is laughing at me

ctx.x: They couldn’t notate the use of the color on the plunger?

That’s the reason I have a book out now, a method of the plunger for trumpets and trombones. That’s the reason I have this. Because now I get in the studio and I can’t play what they have written down here for me. And here all this money is going out the window. And I’m looking at Fred Astaire, we’ll go a few bars and they had to cut because I had messed up, because I wasn’t getting exactly what was the way it was designed for him to do for he and Barrie Chase. And he’d go down on his knees and wheel around and…

this until I finally said, and then Count Basie, he never comes out of the booth, now he comes around to me and he says, “what’s wrong, Fab?” And I say, “oh, Chief,” I said, “I can’t read this because the positions that I played with my plunger on that date I can’t get with, and it’s not written like I played it, and so I don’t know what to do.” And they were getting very worried, because here we had went into the studio like 8:00 that morning and here it is going on 11:30 and we hadn’t accomplished the first…
